title: Version bisection and tenant quarantine upgrade playbook
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines an operational playbook and IaC changes for automated, tenant-aware control-plane upgrades in VPC/private deployments. The goal is to enable fast detection and isolation of regressions introduced by a control-plane version while minimizing blast radius across tenant fleets. Key innovations: (1) a version bisection promotion strategy that rapidly narrows down faulty version ranges by halving cohorts, and (2) a tenant quarantine mechanism that automatically isolates affected tenants, redirects their control-plane interactions to a vetted fallback version, and captures enriched diagnostics for postmortem.

Scope of work:
- Terraform: extend existing private-controlplane modules with explicit upgrade_strategy, cohort_definition, health_probe_config, and quarantine_policy fields. Add a new stateful resource to record per-tenant promotion state and bisection checkpoints.
- Orchestration: implement a bisection coordinator in the control-plane operator that can perform cohort halving, evaluate health gates, and trigger roll-forward or staged rollback.
- Health checks: expand health gating to include (a) per-tenant API latency P95, (b) error-rate delta vs baseline, (c) KV-cache miss-rate regressions, and (d) control-plane RPC saturation.
- Tenant quarantine: operator flow to mark a tenant as "quarantined" and route its control-plane traffic to a pinned fallback control-plane instance group until diagnostics are collected and a manual or automated remediation is applied.
- Telemetry & alerting: add new metrics (upgrade.promotion_step, upgrade.bisection_index, tenant.quarantine_count, quarantine.reasons) and dashboards and PagerDuty triggers for failures that cross escalation thresholds.
- Runbook & automation: author a documented runbook with automated steps for: staged kickoff, bisection choreography, quarantine diagnostics collection, and recovery validation.

Design notes / trade-offs considered:
- Why bisection? Traditional percentage-based canaries can take multiple steps to isolate a regression when many minor versions are in-flight. Bisection reduces the number of promotion steps from O(n) to O(log n) when we have a contiguous range of candidate versions (e.g., multiple patch iterations). It does add complexity to cohort selection and requires deterministic promotion ordering.
- Quarantine vs immediate rollback: quarantining preserves service for the unaffected majority while shielding the affected tenants and retaining diagnostic context. Immediate global rollback is simpler but has higher customer impact. We implement quarantine as the default when per-tenant impact is detected.
- Terraform state changes: recording per-tenant promotion state in IaC state allows reproducible promotions across operator restarts but requires careful state locking and lifecycle rules to avoid drift. We will document locking requirements and create helper tasks in the module.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Terraform module changes (week 1): add schema for upgrade_strategy (values: cohort, bisection, shadow), cohort_selector (labels/tag rules), and quarantine_policy (max_quarantined, auto_release_delay). Provide migration script to backfill existing tenant records.
2) Operator & coordinator (weeks 2-3): implement bisection coordinator, tie into existing rollout controller, implement tenant quarantine API (CRD/annotated resource) and safe fallback routing.
3) Health gating & telemetry (week 3): implement new probes, wire metrics to observability stack, add dashboards and SLO-based gating rules.
4) E2E tests & chaos (week 4): create test harness to simulate regressions (latency spike, error-rate increase) and validate bisection converges and quarantine triggers.
5) Pilot & production rollout (week 5): pilot on staging tenants, then a small set of production tenants with manual oversight, then enable automated promotion for low-risk channels.

Acceptance criteria:
- Terraform module adds documented inputs: upgrade_strategy, cohort_selector, health_probe_config, quarantine_policy, with examples in README (must be present).
- Operator supports a bisection promotion workflow and exposes a promotion state resource for auditing.
- Tenant quarantine API can be exercised via CLI and UI and correctly routes traffic to fallback instances.
- Telemetry emits upgrade.bisection_index and tenant.quarantine_count and dashboards show promotion progress per-tenant.
- E2E harness validates at least two simulated regressions where bisection isolates offending version within 3 steps and quarantine isolates affected tenants without global rollback.
- Security review completed and signed off (security_review_required flag).

Acceptance tests / test matrix (short):
- Regression scenario: each candidate version introduces an incrementally larger latency bump; validate bisection identifies offending version and quarantines < 5% of tenants.
- Fail-open scenario: coordinator fails mid-promotion; verify idempotent state and safe rollback to last known-good.
- Terraform drift: simulate state mismatch and verify module tooling can reconcile without tenant disruption.

Artifacts / links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Version+Bisection+%26+Tenant+Quarantine+Design
- Operator prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/4218
- Terraform module branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-terraform/tree/feat/upgrade-bisection

Runbook excerpt (concise):
- Kickoff: create UpgradePlan resource with strategy=bisection and versions=[v2026.02.11, v2026.02.18, v2026.02.25]
- Step 0: sanity checks (control-plane health, infra capacity, no active critical incidents)
- Step 1: promote cohort A (50% tenants) to midpoint version; wait 15m; evaluate health probes
- Step 2: if probes pass, promote half of remaining cohort to higher version, else bisect downward and mark quarantines per rule set
- Step Q: when tenant.quarantine triggers, operator pins tenant to fallback, captures diagnostics bundle, and increments quarantine counter. Notify oncall and open automated diagnostics PR.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should quarantined tenant logs be centrally stored in a limited retention bucket for privacy/compliance? (security to weigh in)
- How do we seed initial cohort assignments for legacy customers who do not have new labels? Proposal: create a migration job that assigns legacy cohorts deterministically by tenant ID hash.
- Operational cost: bisection requires more promotion steps for some cases; need SRE cost estimate for manual oversight during pilot.

Estimated risks and mitigations:
- State drift between Terraform and operator: mitigation = state reconciliation tool + stronger state locking and an operator read-only mode when state migration runs.
- False positives in health probes causing unnecessary quarantines: mitigation = require multi-window evaluation and cross-metric correlation before quarantine.
- Data privacy for diagnostic bundles: mitigation = encrypt bundles with tenant-specific KMS keys and limit retention to 7 days by default.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module documented inputs and examples exist
Operator exposes bisection workflow and promotion state resource
Tenant quarantine API routes traffic to fallback instances
Telemetry metrics and dashboards for promotion progress
E2E harness demonstrates isolation within 3 bisection steps
